key_insight: Microscopic impurities nucleate perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can detect and quantify them within seconds.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could help prioritize more stable wide-bandgap perovskite films for scalable tandem solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
Apply machine learning-supported reflected-light image analysis to quantify impurities and track degradation.
evidence_signal: Films with higher impurity density showed faster early degradation, while degradation tracking indicated coupled photochemical and thermochemical contributions.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative detection accuracy or validation across different film compositions and manufacturing conditions.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
